metadata.name: beta_mint
metadata.description: BETA: a token minted against real native-SOL value locked through ipow-conversion's bitcoin->native auction, redeemable in reverse — the first concrete CPI consumer of ipow-conversion (docs/DESIGN_V2.md's Phase 2). Same-chain, single-asset (native SOL) slice of the fuller multi-network basket-backed minting vision documented as Phase 4 (design only).

docs: BETA: a token minted against real native-SOL value locked through
`ipow-conversion`'s bitcoin->native auction, redeemable in reverse —
the first concrete CPI consumer of `ipow-conversion`
(`docs/DESIGN_V2.md`'s Phase 2), and the same-chain slice of the fuller
multi-network basket-backed minting vision documented there as Phase 4
(design only). Never modifies `ipow-conversion`'s own state directly —
every value-moving step goes through a real CPI into its own
instructions, signed by this program's own vault/mint-authority PDAs.

types.name: BasketMintRequest
docs: Tracks a two-hop, cross-chain basket mint: Leg1 (native->bitcoin, locks
the full deposit, claimed by an arbitrageur who's separately completing
the matching Ethereum-side legs) and Leg4 (bitcoin->native, the
self-escrowed return leg that actually funds the vault). BETA only
mints once both Solana-local legs independently resolve with a real,
Solana-verified Bitcoin proof — see `docs/DESIGN_V2.md`'s basket
section for what this does and doesn't guarantee about the Ethereum
side.

types.name: BetaGlobalState
docs: This program's own singleton state. `vault_bump`/`mint_authority_bump`
are stored rather than re-derived every call since both PDAs are used
repeatedly as CPI signers across every instruction in this program (same
convenience `ipow-conversion`'s `Pool.escrow_bump` uses, just singleton
here instead of per-mint since this pass only backs BETA with native
SOL — see `docs/DESIGN_V2.md`'s "BETA: same-chain slice" section).

types.name: Conversion
docs: See `docs/DESIGN_V2.md` for the full design this implements. Two
structural changes from the version that still lives, unmodified,
inside `ipow`:
1. No single fixed `global_state.operator` — `responsible_operator` is
won through a windowed staked auction (`propose_claim_conversion` /
`finalize_claim_conversion` / `reclaim_expired_conversion`), the same
mechanics already proven on `ipow-message-relay`'s
`MessageCommitment`. See this struct's own auction fields below.
2. `token_mint` generalizes `native_amount` from "always native SOL" to
"native SOL if `Pubkey::default()`, else this SPL mint" — every
instruction that moves `native_amount` branches on this once.

fields.name: token_mint
docs: `Pubkey::default()` = native SOL; otherwise the SPL mint this
conversion's `native_amount` is denominated in.

fields.name: extra_tokens
docs: `token->bitcoin` only — up to 3 additional (mint, amount) pairs
beyond the primary `token_mint`/`native_amount` slot, settled by
the same single `bitcoin_amount` proof. Always empty for
`bitcoin->token` and for any single-token `token->bitcoin`
conversion — every instruction's existing behavior is unchanged
when it is.

fields.name: responsible_operator
docs: `Pubkey::default()` until `finalize_claim_conversion` locks in a winner.

fields.name: staked_bond
docs: What the current/winning claimant actually staked.

fields.name: required_bond
docs: Minimum stake to claim; escalates on forfeiture via
`reclaim_expired_conversion`, same rule as `MessageCommitment.
required_bond`.

fields.name: claim_started_at
docs: Start of the current claim window (reset on every reopen).

fields.name: last_claim_at
docs: Timestamp of the most recently accepted claim — `finalize_claim_
conversion`'s quiet-period check counts from this.

fields.name: duty_window_seconds
docs: Duty window length the winning claimant commits to, in seconds —
supplied as part of their claim (like the old design's caller-supplied
`duty_window_seconds`, now part of the bid rather than fixed by the
approving operator).

fields.name: bounty
docs: Forfeited stakes from prior failed attempts on this same conversion —
paid out on top to whichever operator eventually completes it.

types.name: ConversionGlobalState
docs: This program's own minimal global state — independent of `ipow`'s
`GlobalState`, matching `ipow-message-relay`'s `RelayGlobalState`
pattern (own counter, own governance, no shared mutable state across
programs). `governance` only gates network config
(`add_network`/`update_network`) and liquidity provisioning — never the
claiming role, which is the whole point of this redesign.

types.name: MintRequest
docs: One per bitcoin->native `Conversion` this program committed as the
vault, seeded by that conversion's own `tx_id` — the record of who
should receive BETA once it completes, and whether that's already
happened (guards against double-mint).

types.name: Pool
docs: One per `token_mint` (native SOL uses `Pubkey::default()`) — replaces
`ipow::GlobalState`'s single `total_locked_deposits`/`total_reserved_
native`/`total_held_commit_fees` fields, which only worked because every
conversion moved the same native SOL. Also the escrow PDA's own bump:
`seeds = [b"escrow", token_mint.as_ref()]` is this program's real vault
(a `SystemAccount` when `token_mint` is default, an SPL token-account
authority otherwise) — kept per-mint for the same reason liquidity is
tracked per-mint below.

fields.name: total_locked_deposits
docs: native->bitcoin: sum of real user deposits currently held pending
proof or refund.

fields.name: total_reserved
docs: bitcoin->native: sum of `native_amount` self-escrowed by claimants
(`propose_claim_conversion`) for in-flight, not-yet-paid-out
conversions of this mint — a pure aggregate for introspection, not
load-bearing for correctness: each conversion's own escrow is backed
by that specific claimant's own transfer, verified at escrow time via
`transfer_value_in`'s balance-delta measurement, not by this counter.

types.name: RedeemRequest
docs: One per native->bitcoin `Conversion` this program committed as the
vault (`initiate_redeem`), seeded by that conversion's own `tx_id` —
records who burned BETA for it, so that amount can be re-minted back
to them if the redemption never actually completes (the claimant fails
to deliver and `refund_no_proof_native_to_bitcoin` fires instead).

types.name: TokenAmount
docs: One extra token in a `token->bitcoin` bundle, beyond the primary
`token_mint`/`native_amount` slot — see `Conversion.extra_tokens`.
